title: Light: Mirrors and Lenses
seo_title: Light Class 8 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10)
standard_text: Reflection from curved mirrors; concave and convex mirrors and their uses; real and virtual images; convex and concave lenses and their uses; the magnifying glass; refraction and dispersion of light; correcting defects of vision (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 8 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 10: concave and convex mirrors and lenses, real and virtual images, uses of mirrors and lenses, refraction and the colours of white light. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Concave mirrors and convex lenses converge light.
key_sub: Convex mirrors and concave lenses spread light out.
body_html:
How to think about it

A concave mirror curves inwards: held close it gives an enlarged upright image (shaving and dentist's mirrors), and it sends out a strong beam from a bulb at its focus (torches). A convex mirror bulges outwards and always gives a smaller, upright image with a wide view (rear-view mirrors). Real images can be caught on a screen; virtual images cannot.

A convex lens is thicker in the middle and brings light together; it is used in magnifying glasses, cameras and our eyes. A concave lens is thinner in the middle and spreads light out. Light bends (refracts) as it enters glass or water, and a prism splits white light into seven colours.

Example

Rear-view mirror of a car?

wide view, upright image

Answer: a convex mirror

Example

A magnifying glass is…

thicker in the middle

Answer: a convex lens

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up concave and convex mirrors.
  • Thinking a virtual image can be caught on a screen.
  • Calling a magnifying glass a concave lens.

faq.q: What is the difference between a real and a virtual image?
faq.a: A real image can be formed on a screen and is upside down; a virtual image cannot be formed on a screen.

faq.q: Why is a convex mirror used as a rear-view mirror?
faq.a: It always gives an upright, smaller image and shows a wide area behind the vehicle.

the reflector in a vehicle's headlight
items.e: The back of a shiny steel spoon: not used as a concave mirror. The other three are.
